memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then Joshua and all Israel with him went up from Eglon to Hebron and attacked it. They took the city and put it to the sword, together with its king, its villages and everyone in it. They left no survivors. Just as at Eglon, they totally destroyed it and everyone in it. — Josh 10:36-37 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The campaign reaches Hebron, and this city name carries a special weight in the story of God's people. Hebron was deeply connected to the patriarchs. It was near Hebron that Abraham had lived, and there that he and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, Jacob and Leah were buried (Gen 23; 49:31). Now, generations later, God's people take possession of this land so bound up with His promises to their ancestors.

There is something moving in this. Centuries earlier, God had promised this land to Abraham, though Abraham himself never possessed it, living as a stranger in it and owning only a burial plot. Yet God's promise did not fail. Slowly, faithfully, over generations, God was bringing to pass what He had sworn long ago. What Abraham received only by faith, his descendants now saw with their eyes.

This is a beautiful reminder that God keeps His promises across generations, even when the fulfilment takes far longer than a single lifetime. Abraham died without seeing it, trusting God for a future he would not live to witness. And God proved faithful. His timeline is often longer than ours, but His faithfulness never falters.

For us, this steadies our hope. God's character is the same today: He keeps His word, even when fulfilment stretches across years or generations. We may not see every promise realised in our lifetime, but we can trust the God who is always faithful. The New Testament reminds us that those who died in faith, like Abraham, were "still living by faith when they died," and that God has prepared something better for all His people (Heb 11:13, 39-40). What God promises, God performs, in His perfect time.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you trusting God for promises whose fulfilment you may not yet see?
2. How does God's faithfulness to Abraham across generations encourage your hope?
3. Can you rest in God's timing even when it stretches longer than you would like?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You keep Your promises across generations and never fail. Help me trust Your faithfulness even when fulfilment takes longer than I would choose. Amen.
